description:
On the /fly route, the HUD speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for the entire duration of a mission to any outer-planet destination (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto).

Expected: The HUD speed readout should show a finite, physically plausible km/s value (e.g., ~25–35 km/s for heliocentric cruise, varying with distance from the Sun) throughout the entire mission.

Acceptance criteria:
- For a Jupiter mission, the HUD speed readout must not show NaN at any point from departure to arrival. At Earth departure (r≈1 AU) the value should be physically plausible for a transfer to Jupiter; at cruise (r≈3–5 AU) it should converge to the Jupiter-encounter heliocentric speed. [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid display value. The vis-viva equation produces a finite real number for any valid orbital state.]
- The heliocentric speed computation must use the transfer-ellipse semi-major axis that matches the mission's actual destination, not a hardcoded Earth-Mars value. [repo-data: src/lib/orbital/mission-arc.ts:93 — outboundArc computes a = (R_EARTH_AU + destA) / 2 per destination. src/routes/fly/+page.svelte:952 — heliocentricKms hardcodes (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2 instead of deriving from the mission's destination.]
- The radicand of the vis-viva expression (2/r - 1/a) must be non-negative for all valid spacecraft positions on the mission arc. Currently for outer-planet missions, r > 2 * 1.262 = 2.524 AU makes the radicand negative. [code-invariant: Math.sqrt(negative) is NaN in JavaScript. The transfer semi-major axis for Mars is 1.262 AU, so r > 2.524 AU (which happens early in any outer-planet mission) causes NaN.]
